episodes.title: I Spent the 90s Watching Cults in Chat Rooms. It Changed How I Hunt Treasure.
episodes.description:
In the early 1990s, when online communities were brand new, I was a researcher watching religious cults gather in chat rooms. Text scrolling across a screen...public spaces, so I could just observe and take notes. And I started noticing patterns.

But here's the thing. When I sat down with some of these same people face to face, they told me things they never said in the chat rooms. And when I read their blogs, they wrote like different people entirely. The pattern I thought I'd found...didn't exist. Not the way I thought it did.

There's a name for what saved me from fooling myself. Qualitative researchers call it triangulation, and it goes back to Denzin in 1978, who borrowed it from people who locate things in the physical world using multiple known points.

In this video I walk through what triangulation actually is, how it works in research, and why it matters enormously if you're following a treasure hunt like the John Collins Black hunt...where the designer is almost certainly layering separate storylines that only converge when you stop riding a single strand.

We are so good at fooling ourselves. This is one of the disciplines that helps.
